heuristics: H1: the class walk on H/mu6 (H the 2^20-th powers in Z_r^*, multiplicative steps with 64 multipliers in H) behaves as a random mapping on M = (r-1)/(6*2^20) classes; S = ceil(2 sqrt(13/20 M)) points give a tame-wild collision with probability 1 - exp(-S^2/(4M)) = 0.477954.

H2: the walk advances 4096 records in rounds; detection of a merged pair costs up to 4096 times the merged path's first-distinguished-point delay (mean 2^90), so the budget S + 2^112 loses at most 2 e^-1024. Cap truncation of merged paths loses at most 2^-9; in-trail cycles at most 1.2e-5; the bounded distinguished-point table overflows with probability at most 1.8e-16.

H3: the walk's additions are batched affine additions with an exact reference core (5n-2 core_mul and n core_sqr per batch of n; 382 and 324 instructions per call, measured by call counts); the per-point other work is charged at the exact measured forced maximum, 8646.36 instructions per point, on a path with every digit nonzero and every batch stage occupied.
Lemma (incomplete addition): for windows 0-11 a batched addition never meets P = +-Q (integer argument); for window 12 the coincidence is charged at 2^-100 under a uniform-digit heuristic.
limitations: H1 is an unproved heuristic; the fresh toy runs (4000 trials on 32- and 36-bit prime-order toy groups with the mu6 action) support it at the claim budget, but nothing is tested at production size.
The claimed success 0.40 is below the Wilson 95% lower bound 0.4227 of the fresh toy runs, minus the stated losses (total 0.00197).

The reference unit is the convention's 2000 instructions; the exact measured reference core is 2234 instructions per addition for large batches (about 0.12 bits of score if each addition were charged at its measured core).
The per-point other-work maximum is measured on a forced path (which includes its forcing code, a conservative overcharge); the full-table round matches the reduced-table round exactly.
The restart path uses 16 precomputed exponents in the measurement; fresh sampling is charged as a bound. The distinguished-point cost is an analytic bound.
Peak memory is about 20.7 GB, dominated by the bounded distinguished-point table.
Analytic production cost; no production-size execution. Not a practical attack.
